correctness.summary: The real-root constraint forces the affine trace interval s_lambda to lie wholly above +2 sqrt(beta) or wholly below -2 sqrt(beta). Each branch then admits an endpoint minimax bound: the positive branch is strictly slower than 1-mu/L for positive momentum, and the negative branch is strictly slower than (L-mu)/(L+mu). The zero-momentum minimax case gives equality exactly at alpha=2/(L+mu). The nonnegative-root frontier follows from the positive branch. Deterministic calculations reproduce the formulas and classical Polyak endpoint/interior root pattern.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical sources establish heavy-ball acceleration, scalar root regimes, stability and optimal parameters; Danilova-Kulakova-Polyak document complex interior roots for the classical optimal tuning; Hagedorn-Jarre give an explicit modern spectral-radius treatment. No checked source stated the constrained interval minimax result that all-real-root heavy-ball tuning cannot beat optimal gradient descent, nor the exact nonnegative-root frontier. Full theorem-level text of Torii-Hagan (2002) and Zhang (2015) was not available in the checked sources, so they remain the principal residual coverage risks.

value.summary: The theorem gives a sharp structural boundary between overdamped/real-root interval tuning and robust acceleration: strict improvement over optimal fixed-step gradient descent requires entering a complex-root regime somewhere in the admissible curvature interval. The companion nonnegative-root frontier quantifies the stronger penalty for forbidding modal sign reversal.

limitations: The theorem is restricted to fixed alpha, fixed beta in [0,1), exact gradients, and strongly convex quadratics.
The worst case is uniform over every curvature in a continuous spectral interval; a finite matrix may skip the complex-root subinterval and therefore need not contain an actual complex-root mode.
Only asymptotic modal spectral radius is compared; no monotone finite-time norm guarantee is claimed.
Complex roots are necessary under the interval-robust criterion but are not sufficient for acceleration.
Adaptive or negative momentum, line search, stochastic gradients, nonlinear objectives, Nesterov acceleration, and conjugate-gradient methods are outside the claim.
Full theorem-level text of Torii-Hagan (2002) and Zhang (2015) was not inspected, leaving residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
